data.title: P. Schreiber: Dolná Mariková – Široká, the 2016 archaeological excavation
data.excerpt: In 2016 the Trenčín Museum in Trenčín, assisted by the Hradiská civic association, carried out an archaeological excavation at the hilltop site known as Široká in Dolná Mariková. A metal-detector survey and micro-trenching recovered material from the Eneolithic, from the Púchov culture and from the 9th to 10th centuries, including two iron hoes and an iron key.

children.text: In 2016 the Trenčín Museum in Trenčín, with the assistance of the Hradiská civic association, carried out an archaeological excavation for research and documentation purposes in the village of Dolná Mariková, at an hilltop site known as Široká. The aim of the fieldwork was to verify the archaeological situations and the dating of the site by test trenching, and to rescue metal objects from a site that was being looted. To this end a metal-detector survey was carried out, followed by micro-trenching at the find spots and overall documentation of the situations.

The earliest finds recovered by the excavation belong to the Late Stone Age, to the Late and Final Eneolithic. These are a small number of pottery fragments, some of them decorated with stamped impressions. Finds from a later period date to the so-called Púchov culture, from around the turn of the eras. These too are fragments of vessels, but also metal objects, such as the find of a bronze pendant (fig. 3: 1). The pendant originally served as a bracelet; after it was broken it was reutilised, i.e. used again as the pendant described above. An iron sickle (fig. 2: 2) can likewise be assigned to the period of the Púchov culture. The Early Middle Ages are represented by finds dated within the 9th to 10th centuries.

Among the more notable objects, mention must be made of the find of two iron hoes (fig. 1: 1), which were found during the survey on the slope of a rock crag, in rock scree. Iron knives (fig. 2: 1, 3) can be assigned to the same period.

The survey also recovered iron arrowheads for a bow (fig. 3: 2 – 4). Their dating is problematic: they may be from the earlier period, that of the Púchov culture, as well as from the later medieval period. One arrowhead is remarkable in that it has an iron tang for fixing into the wooden shaft (body) of the arrow strengthened by twisting (fig. 3: 4).

Finally, mention should be made of the find of a key made of iron (fig. 1: 2). The body of the key, like that of the arrowhead, is strengthened by twisting; at the end there is a ring, and the head is in the shape of a “T”. The key was found by survey and subsequent micro-trenching. Similar keys occur from the period of the Púchov culture through to the Early Middle Ages, and so it cannot be said with certainty whether the key belongs to the earlier or to the later occupation.

The find spot of Dolná Mariková – Široká is first mentioned in the archaeological literature by A. Habovštiak in 1972, as “a small plateau with attested medieval fortification” (Habovštiak 1972). More recent literature records occupation at the Široká site from the Late Stone Age, from the protohistoric period and from the Middle Ages (Moravčík 2000; Májsky 2006; Malec 2010; Schreiber 2015).
